paragraphs: This paper investigates why fine-tuning can reduce the amount of data needed for a new task. It studies regression problems with linear teachers, making the relationship between pretraining and downstream learning mathematically tractable. The central question is how to measure whether a source task provides useful preparation for a target task.

The analysis shows that source–target similarity must account for the covariance structure of the target data: how its input features vary together. In linear regression, a low value of the resulting measure can produce substantial reductions in sample complexity under the settings studied. Task similarity therefore depends on the data distribution as well as on the tasks themselves.

For deep linear regression, the authors characterize the preference induced by gradient training starting from pretrained weights. This result shows that network depth also affects the relevant similarity measure. They additionally analyze shallow ReLU models and provide empirical demonstrations using synthetic and realistic data. Together, the results explain specific ways that initialization, architecture, and task relationships can influence fine-tuning’s data efficiency.
neurips-2021-a-theoretical-analysis-of-f.tldr: Theoretical analyses show how task relationships, target-data covariance, and network depth affect the data efficiency of fine-tuning.

paragraphs: The paper studies the optimization landscape of two-layer ReLU networks trained with squared loss on labels produced by a target network. Its focus is spurious minima: locally favorable solutions that do not achieve the global minimum. The authors exploit symmetries in the problem to obtain analytic information for finite input dimensions and neuron counts.

Their tools estimate losses at different minima and characterize the Hessian spectrum, which describes local curvature. Up to corrections of order d to the power minus one-half, most eigenvalues concentrate near small positive constants, while a number proportional to d grow linearly with d. Global and spurious minima have matching spectra to that same approximation order.

This similarity challenges attempts to explain statistical generalization using local curvature alone in the studied setting. The method also identifies exact fractional dimension values at which families of critical points change from saddles into spurious minima. That characterization opens a route to studying how such minima appear and disappear through symmetry-aware bifurcation theory.
neurips-2021-analytic-study-of-families-.tldr: Symmetry-based analysis reveals closely matching local curvature at global and spurious minima in two-layer ReLU networks.

paragraphs: This paper seeks a clearer interpretation of Transformer attention by connecting it to an existing model of associative memory. Attention is an important component of deep learning, but its effectiveness does not by itself explain what kind of computation it performs. The authors use a relationship with Kanerva’s Sparse Distributed Memory to develop that interpretation.

Sparse Distributed Memory is described as a biologically plausible associative memory model. The paper shows that Transformer attention can be closely related to it when particular conditions on the data hold. Those conditions are central to the claim: the connection is conditional, rather than an assertion that every use of attention is equivalent to this memory model.

The authors check pretrained GPT2 Transformers and confirm that the required conditions are satisfied there. This gives the proposed relationship an observed setting in which it applies. They then discuss computational and biological implications of the mapping. The contribution is an explanatory connection that offers another way to understand attention through associative memory.
neurips-2021-attention-approximates-spar.tldr: Under data conditions verified in pretrained GPT2 models, Transformer attention closely relates to Sparse Distributed Memory.

paragraphs: This paper addresses feature collapse in deep vision Transformers: the reduction in feature diversity as information passes through more layers. Rich representations are a major source of these models’ usefulness, so losing diversity with depth works against that capability. The authors theoretically analyze the phenomenon and examine how shortcut connections relate to feature diversity.

Their proposed modification adds learnable paths alongside the existing shortcuts. These augmented shortcuts provide additional parameterized routes through the model. The design follows directly from the paper’s investigation of shortcuts, making the connections themselves a target for improving representations rather than treating them as a fixed architectural detail.

To keep the additional computation modest, the authors implement the augmented paths using block-circulant projections, a structured form of projection. Experiments on benchmark datasets report about a 1% accuracy increase for state-of-the-art vision Transformers without an obvious increase in parameter counts or floating-point operations. These findings support the usefulness of changing shortcut structure while keeping the overall computational footprint similar in the evaluated models.
neurips-2021-augmented-shortcuts-for-vis.tldr: Learnable paths added alongside Transformer shortcuts improve benchmark accuracy with little reported increase in model size or computation.

paragraphs: CAM-GAN tackles continual data generation, where a generative adversarial network must accommodate a sequence of tasks. The approach separates parameters into a shared global set, held fixed across tasks, and task-specific adapters. These adapters transform feature maps to support each task while keeping the amount of added machinery relatively small.

The method also adds a residual bias element by element in the transformed feature space to help stabilize training. To use knowledge from earlier tasks, it measures task similarity through the Fisher information matrix. The authors report that using these similarities improves performance and reduces parameter growth, helping the continually adapted model remain compact.

Experiments on diverse, challenging datasets show better performance than the compared state-of-the-art continual GAN methods with substantially fewer parameters. The generated samples are also reported to help continual learning for discriminative tasks through generative replay. The findings connect efficient adaptation inside the generator to a second use: supplying generated examples that support learning across successive tasks.
neurips-2021-cam-gan-continual-adaptatio.tldr: CAM-GAN combines compact task adapters and task-similarity information to improve continual generation with fewer parameters.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to estimate the average outcome of a new treatment rule from historical data collected under another rule. This is off-policy evaluation. Its focus is continuous treatments, such as selecting a personalized dose, where the available choices cannot naturally be represented by a short list of discrete alternatives.

The proposed method, deep jump learning, builds an adaptive discretization of the treatment space. It combines deep learning with change-point detection operating at multiple scales to construct that discretization. This step is the bridge to existing evaluation methods: after organizing continuous treatments into discrete regions, the method can use techniques developed for discrete treatment decisions.

The approach matters because much of the existing off-policy evaluation literature concentrates on discrete treatments. It provides a way to bring those tools into a continuous setting through a learned representation of treatment choices. The authors support the method with theoretical results, simulations, and an application to Warfarin dosing, addressing both its mathematical basis and its use on a real treatment problem.
neurips-2021-deep-jump-learning-for-off-.tldr: Deep jump learning adaptively discretizes continuous treatments so existing off-policy evaluation methods can estimate outcomes under new treatment rules.

paragraphs: Molecular graph networks can benefit from directional information, but the true positions of atoms are often unavailable or too costly to obtain. This paper introduces synthetic coordinates so models can use geometric information without requiring the actual molecular configuration. The aim is to extend the usefulness of directional message passing to coordinate-free inputs.

The authors propose two sources of synthetic distances. One uses bounds describing a rough range of possible molecular configurations. The other derives distances from the graph using a symmetric form of personalized PageRank. They also introduce a transformation that allows ordinary graph neural networks to use both distance and angular information in directional message passing.

On ZINC, this transformation reduces the error of a standard graph neural network by 55% in the reported experiment. Incorporating synthetic coordinates into SMP and DimeNet++ also produces state-of-the-art results on ZINC and coordinate-free QM9. These findings show that useful directional structure can be supplied without access to true atom positions in the evaluated prediction tasks.
neurips-2021-directional-message-passing.tldr: Synthetic distances enable directional molecular graph networks without true atom coordinates and improve prediction on the evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: Sparse networks promise cheaper training, but learning which connections to use can still require dense computation. This paper identifies gradient estimation for structure parameters as a source of that problem: earlier approaches may need dense backward passes even when the network itself is sparse. The proposed method keeps both forward and backward computation sparse.

The authors formulate training as continuous optimization under a global sparsity constraint and separate weight updates from structure updates. Weight learning uses the usual chain rule while exploiting the sparse network. Structure learning instead uses a variance-reduced policy-gradient estimator that requires two forward passes and no backward pass for that update.

This separation addresses the computational cost of adapting the sparse structure itself. The paper proves that the proposed estimator has bounded variance, providing a theoretical property of the estimation method. Experiments on real-world datasets show more effective training acceleration than previous methods, with speedups reaching an order of magnitude. That upper-end result is an experimental finding, rather than a uniform speed guarantee.
neurips-2021-efficient-neural-network-tr.tldr: Separate weight and structure updates enable fully sparse training, with reported speedups reaching an order of magnitude.

paragraphs: A single federated model can perform well on average while serving some clients very poorly because their data differ. This paper approaches personalization through an explicit statistical assumption: each client’s data distribution is a mixture of unknown underlying distributions. That assumption gives a common basis for describing relationships among clients’ learning tasks.

The authors show that this mixture formulation encompasses most existing personalized federated learning approaches and leads to algorithms resembling expectation-maximization. They develop versions for both client-server collaboration and fully decentralized settings. The formulation also supplies a principled route to personalized models for clients that were absent during training, extending personalization beyond the original participating group.

To study convergence, the paper introduces a federated surrogate optimization framework that may be useful beyond these particular algorithms. On federated learning benchmarks, the proposed approach achieves higher accuracy and fairness than the compared state-of-the-art methods. These results support using a distributional model of client differences to guide personalization, alongside the paper’s theoretical analysis of the resulting learning procedure.
neurips-2021-federated-multi-task-learni.tldr: Modeling client data as mixtures yields personalized federated algorithms with convergence analysis and improved benchmark accuracy and fairness.

paragraphs: This paper asks where the identity of a decision-maker matters most. People can respond differently to similar circumstances, such as doctors choosing initial treatments or judges handling particular cases. The goal is to identify types of situations with especially strong disagreement across decision-makers, rather than describing only an overall level of variation.

The authors formulate the task causally: they seek a region of contexts where assigning a different decision-maker has a large effect on the decision. Their algorithm searches for such a region by maximizing an objective calculated from observed data. A generalization bound accompanies the method, connecting its empirical search to a theoretical assessment of performance.

In a semi-synthetic experiment, the algorithm accurately recovers the intended region of heterogeneity compared with baselines. Applications to real healthcare datasets also uncover variation consistent with existing clinical knowledge. These findings support the usefulness of locating disagreement within particular contexts, making it possible to examine where decision-maker differences are concentrated rather than treating all cases as equally affected.
neurips-2021-finding-regions-of-heteroge.tldr: A causal formulation and search algorithm identify contexts where changing the decision-maker has a large effect on decisions.

paragraphs: This paper examines prediction on unusual examples or uncommon subgroups within a training distribution. These out-of-context cases can expose failures that ordinary evaluation does not adequately characterize. The authors introduce a framework that brings together existing approaches to measuring this behavior and makes the role of context explicit in benchmark construction.

They show how rich auxiliary information can identify candidate out-of-context examples already present in datasets. The resulting NOOCh suite consists of naturally occurring challenge sets. Different definitions of context produce sets that probe different kinds of failure, so the benchmark construction process becomes a way to ask more specific questions about model behavior.

The experiments compare tradeoffs among learning approaches across these challenge sets. They also show that benchmark design choices can lead to different conclusions about out-of-context performance. The practical message is that a result depends in part on which notion of unusualness the evaluation captures. NOOCh provides a framework and concrete challenge sets for examining those distinctions systematically.
neurips-2021-identifying-and-benchmarkin.tldr: NOOCh uses naturally unusual dataset examples to show how definitions of context affect conclusions about model performance.

paragraphs: Extreme multilabel classification must handle very large sets of possible labels, potentially numbering in the millions. Partitioning labels into clusters helps make this manageable, but assigning every label to exactly one cluster can be restrictive. A label may carry multiple meanings, as with Apple referring to either a fruit or a brand.

This paper treats label assignment as an optimization problem aimed at maximizing precision. The resulting algorithm permits flexible, overlapping clusters, allowing a label to participate in more than one grouping. The authors also propose alternating between updating cluster assignments and updating model parameters, so the organization of labels can adapt alongside the classifier.

Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that the method can separate the different modes of ambiguous labels. The authors report state-of-the-art results on four extreme multilabel classification benchmarks. These findings support making the partition structure responsive to the downstream prediction objective: scalability need not depend on forcing every label into a single mutually exclusive semantic group.
neurips-2021-label-disentanglement-in-pa.tldr: Optimizing overlapping label clusters helps disentangle ambiguous labels and improves extreme multilabel classification on four benchmarks.

paragraphs: This paper develops a scalable way to approximate the evolution of probability distributions through Wasserstein gradient flows. In this perspective, certain diffusion equations become gradient descent over functionals of distributions. The JKO scheme turns that evolution into a sequence of implicit optimization steps, but solving each step can be computationally difficult.

The proposed method represents the JKO steps using input-convex neural networks and optimizes them through stochastic gradient descent. This brings a neural-network-based approximation to the core computational problem. Unlike the previous approaches discussed in the abstract, it does not require dividing the domain into a grid or simulating a collection of particles.

The representation allows the authors to sample from the evolving distribution and evaluate its probability density at each time step. They demonstrate the method on Fokker–Planck diffusions and apply it to sampling from unnormalized densities and nonlinear filtering. These applications connect the mathematical flow formulation to machine learning tasks that require practical access to changing probability distributions.
neurips-2021-large-scale-wasserstein-gra.tldr: Input-convex neural networks make Wasserstein diffusion steps scalable while supporting sampling and density evaluation over time.

paragraphs: This paper proposes a generative vision Transformer for detecting salient objects in images. Alongside its image-processing network, it uses latent variables governed by a learned energy-based prior. The purpose of this prior is to describe the latent space more expressively than the simple isotropic Gaussian distributions used by the generative approaches discussed in the abstract.

The Transformer and prior are trained jointly through maximum likelihood estimation using Markov chain Monte Carlo. Because the latent prior and posterior are intractable, the method uses Langevin dynamics to perform the required sampling. The latent-variable formulation also allows the system to produce a confidence-related uncertainty value for each image pixel.

The authors apply the framework to both ordinary color images and images accompanied by depth information. Their experiments report accurate saliency predictions and meaningful uncertainty maps consistent with human perception. The contribution therefore combines object saliency estimation with an indication of where the model is less certain, supported by a more expressive learned distribution over its latent variables.
neurips-2021-learning-generative-vision-.tldr: A generative vision Transformer with a learned energy-based prior produces accurate saliency predictions and meaningful pixel-level uncertainty maps.

paragraphs: This paper studies how cooperating agents can develop a shared basis for communication. A common language might emerge through repeated attempts to coordinate, but that consensus process can require many rounds of trial and error. The authors investigate another source of common meaning: representations grounded in what agents observe in their environment.

Their method uses autoencoding, a standard representation-learning approach, to construct those grounded representations. Agents broadcast the resulting representations and learn to interpret and respond to one another’s messages. This makes observation-based representation learning part of the communication mechanism, connecting what agents say to information about the world they are interacting with.

Across a variety of multi-agent communication environments, the authors find that this simple approach supports strong task performance. Their result establishes autoencoding as sufficient for obtaining a grounded common language in the settings evaluated. It highlights a practical connection between representation learning and decentralized coordination: useful communication can build on learned descriptions of observations rather than relying entirely on an unconstrained consensus process.
neurips-2021-learning-to-ground-multi-ag.tldr: Agents can use autoencoded observations as a grounded common language that supports strong decentralized coordination.

paragraphs: This paper estimates the position and orientation of previously unseen objects belonging to known categories from individual 3D point clouds. The proposed learning framework requires neither ground-truth pose annotations nor CAD models nor multiple views during training. It addresses the annotation burden of category-level pose estimation by learning shape and pose together.

The method separates the problem into an invariant shape reconstruction module and an equivariant pose estimation module. Invariance supports a consistent representation of shape, while equivariance links pose estimates to changes in the input’s position and orientation. SE(3)-equivariant point-cloud networks enable this separation. Aligned shape reconstructions establish a category-level reference frame without annotations.

Experiments cover complete and partial point clouds from ModelNet40 as well as real depth observations from NOCS-REAL 275. The pose estimator reaches accuracy comparable to some fully supervised methods. The findings show that the proposed geometric structure can supply useful training guidance, allowing category-level pose estimation without the pose labels and additional supervision excluded by this setup.
neurips-2021-leveraging-se-3-equivarianc.tldr: Geometric invariance and equivariance enable self-supervised object pose estimation without pose labels, CAD models, or multiview supervision.

paragraphs: This paper trains hierarchical Transformers to generate hardware circuits from high-level logical requirements expressed in linear-time temporal logic. The task is circuit synthesis: producing a circuit that implements a specification. It is an established algorithmic challenge, and a major obstacle for learning-based approaches is the limited supply of suitable specification–circuit training pairs.

The authors address that obstacle by generating additional paired training data. To make the synthetic specifications resemble human-written ones, they mine recurring patterns from specifications used in synthesis competitions. Those patterns guide data generation, tying the expanded training collection to the kinds of logical requirements that appear in established synthesis problems.

Hierarchical Transformers trained on this data solve a significant portion of the competition problems. They also solve out-of-distribution examples from a recent case study. The findings support pattern-based synthetic data as a useful way to train neural synthesis systems when direct training examples are scarce. The reported successes span both competition-derived tasks and examples beyond the training distribution.
neurips-2021-neural-circuit-synthesis-fr.tldr: Synthetic training pairs built from specification patterns help hierarchical Transformers synthesize circuits for competition and out-of-distribution problems.

paragraphs: This paper extends neural scene representations toward relighting participating media, where light interacts throughout a medium rather than only at opaque surfaces. The authors identify two shortcomings in the approaches they discuss: neglect of participating media and omission of higher-order indirect illumination. Ignoring those indirect contributions can lead to energy loss in rendered results.

Their method learns a neural representation with a complete simulation of global illumination. It estimates direct lighting through ray tracing and handles indirect lighting with spherical harmonics. This combination accounts for indirect illumination without explicitly computing the lengthy sequence of bounces, and the authors state that it avoids the associated energy loss.

Experiments across multiple scenes report better visual quality and numerical performance than the compared state-of-the-art methods. The approach also extends to solid objects with opaque surfaces. The contribution is therefore both a broader treatment of scene materials and a different way to compute lighting, supporting relightable representations that include illumination effects omitted by the methods motivating the work.
neurips-2021-neural-relightable-particip.tldr: A neural rendering method combines ray tracing and spherical harmonics to relight participating media while accounting for higher-order indirect illumination.

paragraphs: This paper investigates overinterpretation: confident classification without input features that provide recognizable semantic support to humans. The authors show that high benchmark accuracy can coexist with this behavior. Networks trained on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet can exploit patterns that are statistically informative even when people do not perceive meaningful evidence for the predicted class.

On CIFAR-10, models make confident predictions after 95% of an image has been masked, leaving pixel subsets without salient features discernible to humans. The authors introduce Batched Gradient SIS to discover sufficient input subsets on complex datasets. Using it, they also show that ImageNet border pixels can suffice for training and testing.

The retained pixels are unmodified, distinguishing this phenomenon from adversarial manipulation of pixel values. The patterns are valid statistical signals within the benchmark, which explains how they can support high accuracy while raising concerns about deployment fragility. Experiments find that ensembling and input dropout can each mitigate overinterpretation. The results expose a gap between successful benchmark prediction and the semantic evidence humans expect a classifier to use.
neurips-2021-overinterpretation-reveals-.tldr: Accurate image classifiers can rely confidently on sparse, semantically unrecognizable pixel patterns, revealing failures hidden by benchmark accuracy.

paragraphs: PettingZoo provides a shared Python interface for a diverse collection of multi-agent reinforcement learning environments. Its goal is to make research easier to exchange, reproduce, and access, following the role that Gym played for single-agent learning. A common interface lets researchers work with different environments through the same basic interaction framework.

The paper also introduces the Agent Environment Cycle, or AEC, game model that underlies the interface. This is a conceptual contribution as well as a software design choice. The authors argue that popular game models do not adequately describe games commonly used in multi-agent learning, creating a mismatch between the formal model and the environment being implemented.

Case studies of major problems in popular environments support the argument that this mismatch can encourage serious, difficult-to-detect bugs. The authors present AEC as a way to address those problems. PettingZoo therefore combines reusable research infrastructure with a proposed improvement in how multi-agent environments are modeled, aiming to make their behavior easier to represent consistently.
neurips-2021-pettingzoo-gym-for-multi-ag.tldr: PettingZoo pairs a common multi-agent environment API with a game model designed to address subtle environment-modeling bugs.

paragraphs: This paper examines why stochastic depth acts as a regularizer in residual neural networks. Regularization aims to improve generalization by limiting overfitting, and stochastic depth had already shown useful performance across tasks. The authors focus on the theoretical understanding of that technique, seeking to explain the effects behind its observed success.

Their approach combines perturbation analysis with signal propagation analysis. These provide complementary perspectives: one examines the effects of perturbations introduced during training, while the other follows how signals travel through the network. Bringing them together allows the authors to investigate different regularization effects of stochastic depth within a shared analysis.

The analysis leads to principled guidelines for selecting survival rates, the probabilities governing which residual components remain active during stochastic-depth training. This connects the theoretical study to a concrete training choice. The contribution is an explanation of regularization behavior that informs how the method is configured, giving a mathematical basis for choosing an important aspect of the training procedure.
neurips-2021-regularization-in-resnet-wi.tldr: A combined theoretical analysis explains stochastic-depth regularization and yields guidelines for choosing survival rates.

paragraphs: ResT is a multiscale vision Transformer designed as a general-purpose backbone for image recognition. The paper modifies attention, positional encoding, and patch embedding to improve efficiency and flexibility. These changes address how the network represents images at different stages as well as how much memory its attention mechanism requires.

Its attention module uses depth-wise convolution to compress memory and introduces interactions across attention heads while preserving their diversity. Positional encoding takes the form of spatial attention, allowing arbitrary image sizes without interpolation or fine-tuning for that purpose. Patch embedding uses stacked, overlapping strided convolutions on the token map instead of straightforward tokenization at each stage.

The authors evaluate ResT on image classification and downstream tasks, reporting substantial improvements over the recent state-of-the-art backbones used for comparison. The findings support the combined architecture as a useful visual feature extractor. Its significance lies in bringing several design decisions together: economical attention, flexible handling of image dimensions, and overlapping image representations within a multiscale Transformer.
neurips-2021-rest-an-efficient-transform.tldr: ResT combines efficient attention, flexible positional encoding, and overlapping convolutional embeddings in a strong multiscale vision backbone.

paragraphs: Bayesian neural networks need practical approximations to distributions over their parameters. This paper addresses the tension between making those approximations expressive and keeping inference computationally manageable. It focuses on the restrictive factorized structure of dropout-based posterior approximations, which limits the statistical dependencies they can represent.

The proposed Variational Structured Dropout method applies an orthogonal transformation to variational Gaussian noise. Learning this structured noise representation introduces dependencies into the approximate posterior while maintaining manageable complexity. The authors also provide a theoretical account showing that the method resolves pathologies of earlier Variational Dropout approaches and supports a standard Bayesian interpretation.

The analysis further identifies an adaptive regularization term with properties that contribute to improved generalization. Experiments on standard benchmarks report effectiveness over state-of-the-art variational methods in predictive accuracy, uncertainty estimation, and detection of out-of-distribution inputs. Together, the theory and experiments support adding structure to the approximation as a way to improve both predictions and the uncertainty information accompanying them.
neurips-2021-structured-dropout-variatio.tldr: Variational Structured Dropout learns dependencies in Bayesian posterior approximations, improving prediction and uncertainty-related performance on standard benchmarks.

paragraphs: This paper studies recognition settings in which the objects themselves can be redesigned. That capability changes the available solution space: object design becomes something that can be optimized for machine perception. The authors develop a framework for creating objects that a deep vision system is intended to classify confidently.

The approach uses deep networks’ unusual sensitivity to changes in their inputs as a design opportunity. Object modifications are optimized to support recognition, producing what the paper calls robust objects. The relevant assumption is concrete: the application must permit changes to the design of what is being recognized. Within that setting, the framework makes recognizability an explicit design objective.

The authors report improved performance on standard benchmarks, in a simulated robotics environment, and in physical-world experiments. These results demonstrate the approach across multiple evaluation settings, including actual physical objects. The contribution is a way to incorporate the vision model into object design, using its response to input changes to guide modifications that improve recognition in the tested settings.
neurips-2021-unadversarial-examples-desi.tldr: Optimizing object designs for confident recognition improves vision performance in benchmark, simulated robotics, and physical-world experiments.

paragraphs: Strategic classification studies prediction when people adapt their behavior in response to a deployed model. A common formulation places the decision-maker first: it selects a model, then strategic agents respond optimally. This paper questions that fixed order by allowing both the decision-maker and the agents to learn and adapt over time.

The authors show that the relative frequencies of adaptation can determine who effectively leads. A decision-maker updating faster than the agents can reverse the conventional arrangement, making the agents the leaders and the decision-maker the follower. The order of play thus emerges from learning dynamics rather than being determined solely by who initially deploys the model.

In standard learning settings, the authors observe that this reversal can benefit both sides. They further show that a decision-maker able to choose its update frequency can induce dynamics converging to Stackelberg equilibria with either leadership order. The findings make update frequency a substantive strategic choice: it can influence both the interaction’s structure and which equilibrium the learning process approaches.
neurips-2021-who-leads-and-who-follows-i.tldr: Relative learning speeds can reverse leadership in strategic classification, and choosing update frequency can steer convergence to either order of play.
